Moreover, batteries have their environmental challenges. By contrast capacitors are lighter and today, power capacitors have the capacity of one to ten megajoules. But for capacitors, the discharge curve drops to 50% by only discharging 75% of its energy. That is why power capacitors can only be used as direct discharge systems for short bursts of energy. pitch_summary: Magnefy is a Stanford spin-out that provides low-cost, non-invasive magnetic sensing and AI-driven digital twin technology for predictive maintenance of critical power infrastructure such as transformers and switchgear, enabling early detection of anomalies months before failure.
investment_thesis_one_liner: Magnefy disrupts grid asset management by combining high-fidelity magnetic sensors with AI to offer a scalable, low-cost predictive maintenance solution for the aging electrical grid.
rationale: Magnefy offers a high-leverage hardware-enabled software model that solves the critical 'brownfield' problem of aging infrastructure through non-invasive, low-cost sensing and proprietary AI. vc_dossier.plain_english_summary: Magnefy builds sensors that act like a 'Check-Engine Light' for the high-voltage power grid. This allows power plants and data centers to fix equipment before it explodes or causes a blackout.
vc_dossier.macro_trend: The Electrification of Everything and AI Power Demand. As the grid ages and data centers consume record amounts of power, a single hour of unplanned downtime can cost over $100,000. Magnefy addresses the urgent need for grid reliability as demand outstrips the current infrastructure's health.
vc_dossier.analogy: The 'Fitbit' for Power Transformers.
vc_dossier.moat_description: Magnefy's defensibility comes from its proprietary Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) magnetic sensors and custom 'Edge AI.' These sensors capture 250x more high-frequency data (up to 50MHz) than standard tools, allowing them to detect 'hidden' signals of failure that competitors miss, all without needing to turn off the power for installation.
